The skill library

Every rule I work by, in a file the agent opens on its own

and where it fires

A skill is one standard plus a line saying when to read it. The line is the trigger; the file is the rule. 29 of them, mounted from the same canon this site publishes, so the library and the standards cannot disagree.

Install the set npx skills@latest add tjakoen/skills

29 skills · generated from the standards · one source, two projections

How a skill fires

1

The line is the trigger

Every skill carries a one-line when: read this before drafting a note, before a commit, before an audit. The agent matches the task against that line, and only then opens the file.

2

The file is the rule

The body holds the bar: the checks, the examples, the failure it prevents. One file, read in full, so the rule arrives with its reasons instead of a summary of them.

3

The loop is where it fires

A session orients, decides, plans, builds, verifies and closes. The router says which standard owns the stage; the stage says when to open it.

A surprise in verify goes back to decide. The steps are not a waterfall; the stages are the order, and the loop is inside them.

The line under the name decides whether the file is opened.

Every when is written as a command, because that line is the only thing an agent reads before choosing. A vague one is a skill nobody opens, which is why the router exists for the tasks that fit two.
